title: Past Test: COMP 311 Theory Test 1 (9 Oct 2024, 70 marks)

questions.q: State 2 disadvantages of using arrays to store information.
questions.model: 1) Fixed size: it cannot grow or shrink after creation. 2) Holds only one data type (homogeneous). Bonus: inserting or deleting in the middle means shifting elements manually.

questions.q: With the aid of a diagram, state 3 stages of Java execution of a program, from the time of writing the code until execution.
questions.model: Diagram: Source code (.java) --javac--> Bytecode (.class) --JVM--> Running program. Stages: (1) write source code; (2) compile with javac into bytecode; (3) the JVM loads and executes the bytecode.

questions.q: Explain the difference between method overloading and method overriding.
questions.model: Overloading: same class, same name, DIFFERENT parameter lists, resolved at compile time. Overriding: subclass replaces an inherited method with the IDENTICAL signature, resolved at run time (runtime polymorphism). Overloading cannot differ by return type alone; overriding needs inheritance.

questions.q: State the difference between a double and a float variable in Java.
questions.model: double: 64 bits, about 15 digits of precision, the default decimal type. float: 32 bits, about 6-7 digits, literals need the f suffix (3.14f).

questions.q: Write a method that takes 2 double variables (a and b) and returns the answer to a divided by b.
Write a method called isPalindrome which takes a String as a parameter and returns true if it reads the same from either side (dad, mum), otherwise false.

hello.txt contains 5 numbers on one line: 22 33 44 55 66. Write a void method (not a class) called process, taking the file path as a parameter, that goes through the file and prints the sum of all the numbers. Deal with any exception that may be thrown.
Use the table to write a switch case statement: Monday, Tuesday -> "unwind"; Wednesday -> "break"; Thursday -> "Ladies Night"; any other day -> "party".
Create a class that represents a football team. The class FootballTeam should be accessible from any package.
Add fields for name of the team, number of wins and number of losses, which cannot be accessed outside the class.
Write a constructor that accepts the name, wins and losses and sets the properties. It should be accessible from any package.
Write a second constructor that takes only the name; set wins and losses to 0. Accessible from any package.
Write 3 methods that return the name, the number of wins and the number of losses. Accessible from any package.
Write a method to increase wins by 1 and another to increase losses by 1. These methods should only be accessible from INSIDE the football package.
questions.model:
void addWin() { wins++; }      // no modifier = package-private
void addLoss() { losses++; }

questions.q: Write a method that returns true when a team has a good record, meaning more wins than losses. Accessible from any package.

Add a main method and, within it: (a) construct a FootballTeam named "AITI" with 3 wins and 5 losses [2]; (b) call the good-record method and print the result [2]; (c) make three calls to the method that increases wins by 1 [3]; (d) call the good-record method again and print the result [2].
